init.title: Claim the engine lease
init.imperative: The worktree, the .agent-work directory, and this spine.json already exist by the time you load: your dispatcher (the Admiral for a delegated run, the human for an interactive one) stood them up per references/stand-up-work-area.md before handing you this spine path. You do not scaffold anything here -- claim the engine session lease on this spine so a resumed or duplicated parent cannot concurrently drive it: call the spine_lease MCP tool with action=claim, claimed_by=commander, worktree=. (add force=true and reason="resuming this run" if a stale prior lease blocks you) -- this is your own spine (the one this process's door is bound to), so the door needs no session id argument, it reads SPINE_SESSION from its own environment.

postconditions.statement: engine session lease claimed for this spine (commander owns the state)

context.title: Load baseline context
context.imperative: Read your inherited global doctrine (this skill's references/global-orchestrator.md and references/global-everyone.md), then the project deltas: docs/agents/ORCHESTRATOR_CONTEXT.md, docs/agents/GLOSSARY.md, docs/agents/engine-config.json. Where the repo carries no docs/agents/ overlay at all (e.g. a skill-source repo), substitute the closest repo doctrine you can find (README, CONTRIBUTING, top-level docs) and record the substitution — do not treat those paths as guaranteed to exist. Before you open any source file, resolve and read the map input: run python <commander-skill-dir>/scripts/map_orient.py orient --root <repo-root> --work-id <work-id>. On RESOLVED, read the entrypoint it names and the packets, overlays and decision anchors it routes you to for the area the ask touches, and treat every later source read as confirming a frame the map already gave you rather than building one out of code. On DEGRADED, re-run the same command with --substitute PATH (what you read instead of a map — it is hash-pinned into the receipt) --unmapped TEXT (what stayed unmapped) --escalation TEXT (what you are escalating, and to whom), and get that on the record before any source read: degraded is a declared reading, never a licence to start from code. The tool probes a fixed fallback order — README.md, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, a docs/ index — and labels a substitute it found there as verified by the filesystem rather than merely asserted by you. The anchor of this instruction is the point: 'before you open any source file' is an act you cannot postpone, whereas a map-first imperative anchored to a late artifact (the gate plan, which is authored at the END of a long run) is satisfied by a run that crawls source for fifty calls, reads the map afterwards, and has complied exactly — that is measured behaviour, not a hypothetical. This read is the map-first input the mission frame and plan are built from. Attest c1.

postconditions.statement: orchestrator context, glossary, engine config loaded; current map read for the affected area where architecture artifacts exist

the orientation contract is satisfied -- RESOLVED, or a DEGRADED verdict discharged with hash-pinned substitutes AND the unmapped gap AND an escalation -- recorded at the context step, which precedes understand and plan. Ordering itself is NOT machine-verifiable from a receipt: nothing in a receipt distinguishes a run that resolved the map first from one that crawled fifty files and then wrote an identical receipt. Ordering lives in this step's imperative ('Before you open any source file') and in the report-only ordering audit, never in this check. This gate is a regression floor so map-IGNORING cannot silently return; it is NOT the fix for map-LATENESS (measured sensitivity 0/4, specificity 0/1). Gate-vs-report is a flag flip: adding --report-only to 'python <commander-skill-dir>/scripts/map_orient.py verify-orientation --root <repo-root> --work-id <work-id>' turns this gate into a non-blocking report without rewiring the step.

understand.title: Understand the ask
understand.imperative: In your own context (interactive: the interrogator reaches the human), load constellation-interrogator and drive interrogation.json with the request, context, and commander starting questions; frame the ask map-first against the affected capabilities, structural anchors, and governing constraints/decisions read at context, and flag any low-confidence/stale/disputed map area the ask depends on. Save the consolidated problem statement. Confirm it with the human. In delegated mode (running from an Admiral launch order, no reachable human), reconcile the ask against the frozen launch order instead of interrogating a human, and satisfy c1 by attaching a user-decision evidence item citing the launch order (the spine_evidence tool with action=attach, task_id=understand, evidence_type=user-decision, fields={cite: 'LAUNCH_ORDER:Mission'}); take a genuine gap to the Admiral — float a decision outside latitude, or query for missing context — per Stop Conditions. See the commander skill's Delegated/autonomous mode.

postconditions.statement: problem statement and protected intent confirmed

plan.title: Author the gate plan
plan.imperative: Map-first: BEFORE authoring execute.json, produce a mission frame from the map input the context step resolved, using templates/MISSION_FRAME.template.md (intent; affected capabilities; relevant examples/events; structural anchors; governing constraints/assumptions; decision anchors and decision pressure; claims/evidence surfaces; map confidence/staleness/disputes; out of scope). Write it to .agent-work/<work-id>/MISSION_FRAME.md — that exact path is what the c6 gate reads, so a frame parked anywhere else reads as no frame at all. For a trivial local/mechanical change where the map adds nothing, shrink or skip the frame and say so in its intent; c6 is waivable, so take that escape as a RECORDED waiver (the spine_evidence MCP tool with action=waive, task_id=plan, condition_id=c6, which=postconditions, authority=human, reason='...') rather than as a silent skip. The c6 gate runs map_orient.py verify-frame over that file: every anchor id the frame cites must exist in the map inventory the context step resolved, or — when context came back DEGRADED — must be one of the substitutes the receipt hash-pinned there, so the frame is compared against a committed prior declaration instead of a same-breath assertion. Know what that check is and is not, and do not overclaim it: it is a regression floor so map-IGNORING cannot silently return, not the fix for map-LATENESS. Measured against this epic's baseline five runs it has sensitivity 0/4 and specificity 0/1, and it inherits the late-anchor defect it was built next to, because anchors-in-a-late-frame is compliance without sequence. The load-bearing map-first anchor is at the context step ('before you open any source file'), which is why verify-orientation is gated there and verify-frame is gated only here. Do NOT 'fix' that asymmetry by also running verify-frame at context: no frame exists at context — the step runs before understand and plan — and the only way to make it pass there is to let an ABSENT frame pass, which is exactly the refusal the whole check is built on. If verify-frame ever has to be context-safe, give it a step-scoped mode; never a vacuous pass. For any low-confidence/stale/disputed map area the run depends on, alter the plan accordingly: add a scout/verification gate or surface it to the human as a decision — never author gates that silently trust an unverified map. Surface durable-structure choices as decision candidates per the skill's Decision candidates section rather than choosing alone. Then author the gate plan into execute.json: each gate the smallest reasonable bite, with close criteria, required evidence, and an anchors block cut from the frame. Before the plan-approved checkpoint run plan-alternatives (parallel gate-plan candidates under distinct constraints, via the references/design-it-twice-brief.md contract) and a cold plan critic (reads the candidate plan + mission frame only, no authoring context); both bias-to-yes — any skip is surfaced as a named untaken road — and the panel-vs-single choice is surfaced to the human at plan approval. Get the human to approve it. In delegated mode, satisfy c3 (plan approved) by attaching a user-decision evidence item citing the launch order's frozen plan and scope -- via the spine_evidence MCP tool (action=attach, task_id=plan, evidence_type=user-decision, fields={cite: 'LAUNCH_ORDER:Mission'}); surface a plan-invalidating discovery to the Admiral rather than blocking on the human. See the commander skill's Delegated/autonomous mode.

postconditions.statement: mission frame produced from the current map (or explicitly skipped as trivial) where architecture artifacts exist
execute.json authored, one bounded issue, gates carry anchors cut from the frame
plan approved
plan-alternatives run BEFORE the plan freezes (parallel candidates under distinct constraints converging to one recommendation), or the skip surfaced as a named untaken road
cold plan critic run on the converged candidate plan + mission frame (after alternatives, before plan approval), findings triaged by the human; panel-vs-single choice surfaced at plan approval

the mission frame at .agent-work/<work-id>/MISSION_FRAME.md cites anchors that resolve against the map the context step oriented on (or, when context degraded, against the substitutes the receipt hash-pinned) — an ABSENT frame REFUSES and never vacuously passes. A regression floor against map-ignoring, NOT a check for map-lateness; waive it for a genuinely trivial change so the escape is recorded. Gate-vs-report is a flag flip: append --report-only to turn this gate into a non-blocking report without rewiring the step.

execute.title: Execute the plan
execute.imperative: Before entering this step: ensure context headroom (run a harness compaction command if one is exposed, else rely on harness auto-compaction — either is fine) and reload the constellation-commander skill into this context, confirming it is active; this satisfies p1. Then, before this step and before EACH detached dispatch, (re)write the crash-resume state note at .agent-work/<work-id>/STATE_NOTE.md (step · slug · next command · PID · expected artifact) from .agent-work/templates/STATE_NOTE.template.md, or the bundled skills/workbench/templates/STATE_NOTE.template.md when the project has no .agent-work/templates/ overlay — the PID changes per detach, and the engine refuses to start execute until it is filled (precondition p2). Then drive execute.json gate by gate in this conversation using this skill's gate execution instructions. Dispatch subagents only for the implementer and reviewer tasks within each gate, and NEVER hand-launch a crew: run every implementer/reviewer dispatch through python <commander-skill-dir>/scripts/run_crew.py (foreground/blocking, durable registry, result-artifact verification). Before this step and before EACH crew dispatch, run python <commander-skill-dir>/scripts/recover_crews.py <work-id> and only launch when it reports no unresolved running/resumable/conflicting crew for that work-id/gate/role/worktree; recover (resume) or explicitly abandon/relaunch any it flags. Record completed outcomes, observed-vs-expected wave evidence, and classified discrepancies at .agent-work/<work-id>/REPLAN_INPUT.json as execution proceeds, in the exact fields of ../constellation-replan/templates/REPLAN_INPUT.template.json when this run is reshaping an epic's wave plan, or of ../constellation-replan/templates/RUN_EVIDENCE.template.json when it is one bounded issue under a frozen launch order (no wave, no forecast, no uncertainty register: report what you observed, do not author structure nobody decided -- #594); discrepancies remain evidence and MUST NOT be auto-filed as issues. Run python <commander-skill-dir>/scripts/verify_iterative_role_artifacts.py commander --work-id <work-id>; missing, malformed, or non-G2 run packets refuse execute completion. If a gate proves the plan wrong, surface the decision to the user before continuing. In delegated mode, surface a plan-invalidating discovery to the Admiral (float it) per the commander skill's Delegated/autonomous mode, rather than blocking on the human.

preconditions.statement: plan approved; context headroom ensured and commander skill reloaded into this context
crash-resume state note written before any detached dispatch (step, slug, next command, pid, expected artifact)

postconditions.statement: every gate closed with integrated evidence
the run's REPLAN_INPUT.json returns observed execution discrepancies/evidence through the exact verified G2 input without automatic issue filing

execute.context_headroom_note: #467. Absolute-token context reserve for THIS gate only: the engine subtracts it from both the soft and hard caps before dividing by the model's window, so `execute` may not be BEGUN with less than this much room left below the hard cap. It makes the imperative's existing prose instruction ('ensure context headroom before entering') enforceable, and it can only ever tighten -- no gate can raise a threshold. WHY 30000, and it is a GUESS, revisable in place: `execute` is the run's longest gate and the one that cannot be abandoned halfway, because it drives every crew gate and each crew dispatch costs tens of thousands of tokens. The only observation available was a commander sitting at ~127K fill after a cold resume plus one full three-task gate -- which bounds one gate's marginal cost in the tens of thousands but cannot separate it from the resume baseline. 30K is a round number at the low end of that range: on claude-opus-5 (1M window, 80K soft / 150K hard) it moves execute's begin-work line from 15% to 12% and its advisory from 8% to 5%, while every other gate keeps the shipped default. The named settle experiment (read fill_fraction across completed commander runs at the moment execute was started) is NOT runnable from existing artifacts -- gauge.json keeps only the latest reading and the per-gate context manifests record no fill -- so a later run may revise this number here, in this one place, without re-deriving anything.

reconcile.title: Reconcile the map
reconcile.imperative: Hand the implemented changes to a subagent that invokes constellation-cartographer to fold them into the recorded architecture — this is the default path whenever a packet map exists. Where the run has no packet map (e.g. a skill-source repo with no docs/architecture map), reconcile the structural record directly instead: fold the change into the schema or design doc it actually touches, and where the change touched neither, record a reasoned no-op as compliant rather than blocking on an absent map.

postconditions.statement: map reflects the implemented changes

triage.title: Route future work
triage.imperative: Load the constellation-triage skill into this context. Drive triage on execute.json triage_candidates in this conversation — do not dispatch a subagent. Before creating any issues, present the full list of recommendations to the human and get explicit approval for each issue to be filed. In delegated mode, satisfy c2 (user approved issue creation) by attaching a user-decision evidence item citing the launch order's issue-filing authority (the spine_evidence tool with action=attach, task_id=triage, evidence_type=user-decision, fields={cite: 'LAUNCH_ORDER:Inherited Latitude'}), or float to the Admiral when filing falls outside inherited latitude. See the commander skill's Delegated/autonomous mode.

postconditions.statement: every triage candidate routed or recorded
user approved issue creation

review.title: Review accomplishments with user
review.imperative: Summarize all gates closed, changes implemented, architecture changes reconciled, and triage items routed or filed. Present the full run summary to the user. Get their confirmation before archiving. In delegated mode, satisfy c1 (run summary accepted) by attaching a user-decision evidence item citing the launch order (the spine_evidence tool with action=attach, task_id=review, evidence_type=user-decision, fields={cite: 'LAUNCH_ORDER:Return Shape'}); the Admiral ratifies at the epic return boundary. See the commander skill's Delegated/autonomous mode.

postconditions.statement: run summary accepted by user

feedback.title: Record workflow feedback
feedback.imperative: Before committing, reflect honestly on how this run actually went: how closely you followed the skills, handoffs, and checklists; where you had to improvise or work around the instructions; what was ambiguous, missing, or contradictory; and what would have helped. Include the crew Workflow Feedback harvested at each gN-integrate. A 'none' answer requires a run-specific reason ('none — confirmed after review: <what you checked>'); a bare 'none' does not close this step. Then record what happened as EPISODES: one episode per distinct thing that happened — not one per run, and not a summary — each stating its task-intent, expected-behavior, observed-behavior, impact-cost and workaround. An episode is a record, not a rule: write what you observed, and do NOT write a rule for a future agent to follow — a rule to follow belongs in docs/agents/* and is a human's call. Write the delta to .agent-work/<work-id>/episode-delta.json and apply it deterministically: python <commander-skill-dir>/scripts/apply_episode_delta.py --delta .agent-work/<work-id>/episode-delta.json --store-root episodes. Pass --store-root on every invocation: the writer's default resolves relative to the installed skill directory, so an installed copy would silently build a store at ~/.claude/skills/constellation-commander/episodes — outside the repo — while every gate reported green. Never hand-edit a file under episodes/: that writer is the only write path into it. Then run the capture gate before advancing: python <commander-skill-dir>/scripts/verify_episode_captured.py <work-id> --store-root episodes --phase feedback.

postconditions.statement: this run captured at least one episode: an episode in the store records this work id

archive.title: Archive, commit, and push
archive.imperative: Commit all remaining work, including the episodes from this run under episodes/. That tracked repo-root path is the durable record. Push the branch and open its PR before the final lifecycle call, because c2 and c2b remain prerequisites on this Commander spine. Run the archive-phase capture gate before closing: python <commander-skill-dir>/scripts/verify_episode_captured.py <work-id> --store-root episodes --phase archive. Confirm the branch is clean and merge-ready. The engine mechanically refuses c4 when the staged diff includes suspicious artifacts; if an artifact is intentional, only a human may waive c4 through spine_evidence. Keep the engine lease active while you satisfy c1, c2, c2b, c3, and c4. Attest c3 only when spine_close is the authorized sole final transition for this run. Then call spine_close once with why=<the final understanding>, tree_clean=true, episodes_captured=true, push=false, and open_pr=false. The false publication choices are deliberate because c2 and c2b already proved publication before this call. spine_close advances archive, releases declared child plans and the top-level lease, reaps bindings, and moves the work area into the archive in the existing finish_work order. Do not manually call the final spine_advance, spine_lease release, reap, or filesystem move. If spine_close refuses, fix the named readiness stage and retry the same tool; do not fall back to the retired manual sequence.

postconditions.statement: work area archived and this run's episode captured AND tracked by git, so the record survives this worktree
branch committed and pushed

the work is REACHABLE: this branch has a pull request that is OPEN or MERGED. A merged PR is reachable work; a closed-unmerged one is not, and neither is no PR at all. A terminal spine and a pushed branch describe the run, not the ref -- CI never runs on an unopened branch, and every commander that reached a terminal spine without opening one had to be chased for it. Open the PR even if the work is unfinished; declare FINAL or PENDING in its title and hand the merge up. Two properties of the check text are load-bearing. The branch is derived at CHECK time from the repo root, never resolved at instantiation: init instantiates the spine before it starts the branch, so the branch need not exist yet -- and a literal branch placeholder is not a resolver-owned token, so instantiation cannot catch one and would ship it unsubstituted. The count is compared in the SHELL because the engine's verdict for a command condition is the EXIT CODE and stdout is discarded: gh --jq 'length > 0' prints true or false but exits 0 either way, so that form can never fail.

check.command: test "$(gh pr list --head "$(git -C <repo-root> rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)" --state all --json state --jq '[.[] | select(.state == "OPEN" or .state == "MERGED")] | length')" -gt 0

postconditions.statement: spine_close is authorized as the sole final advance-and-release transition for this run

staged diff carries no suspicious artifacts (oversized files, generated record dumps, disallowed dirs, binary/blob additions, large data files); refuse closeout unless a human waives via the engine override path
